findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() is dead logic that always returns false regardless of the feature toggle
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns `false` in both branches of the following `if`, so the flag check has no effect whatsoever. While the net effect (always disabled) is the security intent of this PR, the code reads as if the feature flag were consulted, which will mislead future maintainers who may 'fix' or extend it. If SQL expressions are meant to be permanently disabled, the function should simply be removed and the call site should unconditionally reject the query; if the flag is meant to matter, the logic is wrong. As written, the `FlagSqlExpressions` feature toggle silently no-ops, and the only user-visible signal is the confusing error at the call site.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is wrong/misleading and is not a proper bad-request error
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression query, they now get `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`. This message is inaccurate: the feature was implemented and has now been deliberately removed/disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). Users who had the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle enabled will get a message that sounds like a transient bug rather than an intentional removal, generating support noise. Additionally, unlike other invalid-query errors in this file's sibling commands (e.g. `errutil.BadRequest("sql-missing-query", ...)` in sql_command.go), this is a bare `fmt.Errorf`, so the API will likely surface it as a 500 internal server error instead of a 400 for what is invalid user input. The message should clearly state that SQL expressions are no longer available and be returned as a bad-request error.

findings.title: UnmarshalSQLCommand path is not guarded by the same disable check as ReadQuery
findings.body: The disable logic was only added to the new `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` path (reader.go, QueryTypeSQL case). The older `UnmarshalSQLCommand` entry point (used when raw nodes are unmarshalled from the legacy query format) still constructs a `SQLCommand` without checking whether SQL expressions are disabled. It currently fails anyway, but only as a side effect: `NewSQLCommand` calls `sql.TablesList`, which calls the stub `DB.RunCommands` that returns "not implemented", and that error is surfaced to the user as `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", "error reading SQL command")` — an error code and message that misrepresent the real cause (feature disabled, not invalid SQL). If the stub DB is ever given a real implementation, this unguarded path would silently re-enable SQL expressions. Both entry points should share a single explicit guard.

findings.title: NoData branch in Execute is dead code — TableData assignment unconditionally overwrites it
findings.body: In `SQLCommand.Execute`, when `frame.Rows() == 0` the code sets `rsp.Values` to a `mathexp.NoData` value, but immediately after the `if` block, `rsp.Values` is unconditionally reassigned to `mathexp.Values{mathexp.TableData{Frame: frame}}`. The NoData result can therefore never be observed, so downstream consumers that distinguish empty frames from NoData (e.g. alerting) get a TableData with zero rows instead. This is a pre-existing bug in a function this PR modifies, and it is worth fixing or removing the dead branch while the function is being touched (it also becomes entirely unreachable now that `QueryFramesInto` always returns an error).

findings.title: No tests added or updated to cover the new "SQL expressions disabled" behavior
findings.body: This PR changes user-visible behavior for the `sql` query type (it now always fails, both via the reader path with the new error and via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` which now fails in `sql.TablesList`), yet no test files are included in the change set. There is no test asserting that a SQL expression query returns an error, that the error is a bad-request rather than a 500, or that the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path is also blocked. Any existing tests covering SQL expression parsing/execution (in pkg/expr and pkg/expr/sql) would exercise the new stub DB and either fail or need updating — none are modified here. Given this is a security fix for CVE-2024-9264, regression tests proving both entry points reject SQL expressions are important to prevent accidental re-enablement.
